braking.scope: Separate structural replay of the stopping impulse at the bumper, with the recorded wheel loads. Rigid fixture force peaks are solver-dependent. Fastener strength and failure were not tested.

boards.simulation: Newton-imported MuJoCo mechanism with two-way Bullet support contacts. Board reaction wrenches drive the pantry world, and its solved board poses update the mechanism collision meshes.
boards.bearing_model: The dry contact model uses coefficient 0.55, gravity-loaded free boards, loose tins and precompressed cloth. The two solvers exchange board poses and contact forces. Bearing faces on fixed furniture are the level patches measured on source meshes. All four car-ramp seats must stay under their respective board. Cabinet and coffee-table joinery is fixed.
boards.capacity_basis: Screen for modeled intact, sealed steel food cans with a wall of at least 0.10 mm. The smallest measured axial collapse in Table 3 was 200 kgf. Use one eighth of this load and further reduce for diameters below 66 mm. This is a comparable-container assumption, not a package rating. No cardboard strength is credited. Cloth is represented in its already-compressed shape; crushing and cloth fiber dynamics are outside the rigid-body model.

cord.scope: Finite cotton cord radius versus visible scene meshes in its swept bounds. Includes head and ladle outside the 13 mm beak grip and 14 mm attachment. Intentional eyelet contacts excluded. Light running cord transmits tension until release. Gravity and a length constraint govern the free end; fiber bending and eye friction are idealized.

twine.scope: The visible basket, keeper band and tied eye follow the solved guided pan. The pulley tendon supplies the resultant force at the eye. Fiber strain, knot friction and tightening are idealized.

moving_mesh_contact_pairs.interpretation: feeder board with its own mounted marble guide
timber stop bedded and fastened to the lower ramp

solids.scope: Triangle mesh overlaps are candidates including support contact, articulated joints, fitted kitchen hardware and authored furniture joinery. Dynamic mechanism meshes tested every half replay frame. Additional moving support meshes were checked at 30 Hz, alongside 960 Hz structural contacts and recorded loads. A finite sampling interval cannot establish a continuous nonintersection guarantee.
solids.source_scope: Contact at the duck soles, fitted supports, bearings, physical impacts, liquid entry and bolted joints is intentional. Face and rack eyelets are also checked using the separate finite-radius cord audit.

duck.note: Gaze is measured from the sourced lens mesh to the moving sugar. The jaw is animated on its source hinge. Ankle, pitch and yaw servos are torque limited.
